extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of CCR units, facility engineers, environmental compliance officers, consultants, and state/federal regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for closing Coal Combustion Residual (CCR) units and CCR management units (CCRMU), including definitions, performance standards, monitoring/engineering methods, required plans, and deadlines for closure/post‑closure activities. Focused on ensuring closure protects human health and the environment where CCR contacts groundwater or contains liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-installation elimination of free liquids (§257.102(d)(2)(i)/(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of any CCR unit or CCRMU that contains liquid must meet the requirements of paragraphs (d)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section prior to installing the final cover system required under paragraph (d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must ensure free liquids are eliminated before final cover installation; EPA extended closure deadlines recognizing the time needed to meet these standards. Suggested alternatives that would be redundant of the definition of 'contains CCR and liquids' were rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of infiltration
rubrics_metrics.description: Infiltration means “the migration or movement of liquid, such as surface water or ground water, into or through a CCR unit from any direction, including from the surface, laterally, and through the bottom of the unit.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA adopted a plain-language, broad definition that includes lateral and bottom flow (not just vertical). The definition aligns with some technical sources and is intended to support protective application of the regulation. EPA rejected technical suggestions that would limit infiltration to vertical flow and found the scope provides adequate notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure vs. corrective action are distinct and independently required
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure standards are designed to ensure waste is dried out and kept dry to prevent leachate formation and future contamination; corrective action provisions set standards/procedures for cleaning up contamination that has already leaked from a unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both sets of requirements must be met; relying on corrective action in lieu of closure is insufficient because closure is preventive while corrective action is remedial (see comparison to 40 CFR 257.97(b)(2)/(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of free liquids and elimination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Free liquids are all “liquids that readily separate from the solid portion of a waste under ambient temperature and pressure” (40 CFR 257.53). Free liquids must be eliminated by removing liquid wastes or solidifying the remaining wastes and waste residues (40 CFR 257.102(d)(2)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to both freestanding liquids and readily separable porewater, regardless of source (sluiced water, stormwater, or groundwater). Where CCR is inundated by groundwater, facilities must take engineering measures to remove groundwater prior to final cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: General performance standard for post-closure infiltration and releases
rubrics_metrics.description: All closures must meet the general performance standard to “control, minimize or eliminate, to the maximum extent feasible,” both post-closure infiltration of liquids into the waste and releases of CCR or leachate to ground or surface waters, and to “preclude the probability of future impoundment of water, sediment, or slurry” (40 CFR 257.102(d)(1)(i),(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General performance standards complement specific technical standards and both must be satisfied for each unit. Demonstrations will be site-specific and may require multiple engineering measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-specific determination to meet performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a particular unit can meet closure performance standards is a fact- and site-specific determination dependent on hydrogeology, unit design and construction, and engineering measures implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities may show compliance by demonstrating a combination of engineering measures and site circumstances (e.g., partial removal of CCR where groundwater intersects only part of an impoundment; installation of controls to stop groundwater flow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering measures to prevent groundwater contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Where groundwater intersects an unlined CCR unit, facilities must take measures (e.g., engineering controls) that will control, minimize, or eliminate post-closure infiltration and releases to groundwater from sides and bottom of the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA references prior guidance and examples of engineering controls to prevent subsurface flow into impounded waste; engineering measures can include dewatering, barriers, extraction systems, or other accepted geotechnical solutions depending on site conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools to identify free liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools that may be used to identify free liquids include soil borings and cone penetrometers to map stratigraphy and characterize geotechnical/hydraulic properties, and properly constructed piezometers, monitoring wells, and vibrating wire piezometers to monitor pore pressures and water levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells and piezometers screened at appropriate locations/depths are prominent instruments for assessing free liquids; water levels under ambient conditions indicate presence/absence of free liquids. Networks of such instruments can be used to demonstrate free liquids no longer exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools and methods to eliminate free liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods used to eliminate free liquids include rim ditches, pumping wells, extraction wellpoints, removal of CCR, solidification, and open excavations for direct observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technologies are currently employed by industry and can both eliminate free liquids and provide evidence of free-liquid conditions. Long-term strategies must consider potential groundwater intrusion and require sustained attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure plan content requirements (§257.102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A written closure plan must be prepared describing whether closure will be accomplished by leaving CCR in place or by removal and include a written narrative describing how the unit will be closed in accordance with the section and how the closure will meet all performance standards, plus a schedule for completing closure activities (40 CFR 257.102(b)(1)/(1)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CCR is left in place, the plan must describe the final cover system and how it will achieve regulatory performance standards; if base intersects groundwater, plan must discuss engineering measures to ensure groundwater removed prior to final cover and measures to meet §257.102(d)(1) (control/minimize/eliminate post-closure infiltration and releases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care plan content requirements (PE-certified) (§257.104(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must prepare a written post-closure plan describing monitoring and maintenance activities, frequency of those activities, point-of-contact during post-closure care, and planned uses of the property. The plan must be P.E.-certified as stated in §257.104(d)(1)(i)-(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certified plan should clearly state the monitoring/maintenance program and responsibilities to ensure long-term protection; deadlines for preparing this plan were extended to allow incorporation of groundwater data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for written closure plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalized a deadline of no later than Wednesday, November 8, 2028 (48 months after the effective date) for owners/operators of CCRMU to prepare the written closure plan required by §257.102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline extended from proposed 12 months to allow incorporation of groundwater quality and flow information, seasonality impacts, and contaminant migration data. Units already closed or eligible for deferral have alternative documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for written post-closure plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalized a deadline of no later than Wednesday, November 8, 2028 (48 months from the effective date) for compliance with the post-closure care requirement in §257.104(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension aligns post-closure plan deadline with closure plan deadline to permit incorporation of groundwater monitoring data and practical feasibility considerations raised by commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to initiate closure
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalized a deadline to initiate closure no later than Tuesday, May 8, 2029 (54 months from the effective date) for CCRMU (extended from the proposed 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation deadline was extended to allow installation of groundwater monitoring systems and collection of baseline samples to inform closure decisions. CCRMU under critical infrastructure may defer initiation until permitting addresses the unit individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to complete closure and extension provisions (§257.102(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators generally must complete closure activities within five years from initiating closure; extensions vary by CCRMU size: units 40 acres or smaller may obtain a maximum 2-year extension; units >40 acres may obtain up to five 2-year extensions (10 years total), with factual justification required for each extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considers closure timeframes for CCRMU comparable to existing surface impoundment closures. Requests for additional or longer extensions must be supported with factual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirement for previously closed or deferred units
rubrics_metrics.description: CCR MU that by the effective date have completed closure with waste in place or have closure eligible for deferral to permitting under §257.101(g) are not required to comply with the written closure plan; instead, owners/operators must provide information on the completed closure with supporting documentation demonstrating the closure meets §257.102(d) performance standards or §257.101(g) standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must support that previously completed closures meet performance criteria and provide evidence for EPA/state review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of porewater and all liquid sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The free liquids requirement applies to both the freestanding liquid in the impoundment and to all readily separable porewater in the impoundment, regardless of whether the porewater originated from sluiced water, stormwater run-off, or groundwater that migrates into the impoundment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering and monitoring plans must account for porewater and not focus solely on freestanding surface liquid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term monitoring, seasonality, and prevention of re-intrusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing successful approaches requires consideration of longer-term variables such as potential groundwater intrusion, seasonality impacts, and the migration of contaminants; full compliance requires successful sustained attainment of performance standards over the long term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators may need long-term engineering measures, continued monitoring, and maintenance applied over time frames necessary to preclude groundwater from intruding back into CCR units after initial elimination of free liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory clarity and legal sufficiency of definitions/performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finds the regulatory definitions (e.g., infiltration) and performance standards are clear and provide adequate notice; they are no more vague than analogous regulations (e.g., §265.111(a)) and have been enforceable over decades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency rejects vagueness claims and notes historic compliance with similar language. Regulated parties must follow the plain-language obligations to control, minimize, or eliminate infiltration and releases.
